source.text: ወኵሉ፡ ቈላት፡ ዕሙቃት፡ ወ*አልቦን፡ ርኅበ፡ እምኵኵሕ፡ ጽኑዕ፡ ወዕፅ፡ ኢይትከል፡ ላዕሌሆን።
source.note: Selected Charles1906 Ge’ez printed p66/PDF104 itself prints the negative ኢ before the planting verb. Raised apparatus15 is not a main-text asterisk. Printed p66 note15 calls the negative added in accordance with G and reports differing Ethiopic evidence and omission elsewhere. This translation retains the selected printed negative, with its unchanged explanation; it does not newly adopt a separate Greek reading. The Greek basis is Charles’s apparatus report: personally inspected facing PDF103 ends within26:4 and does not show Greek26:5. The present followup reviews this bounded editorial-supply/provenance metadata, not a new full source/English acceptance or manuscript certification.

translation.text: All the ravines were deep and narrow[a], of hard rock, and no[b] tree was planted on them.

footnotes.text: Literally, “without breadth.” This describes the ravines, not an additional place.

Charles 1906 printed p66 note15 identifies the negative as an editorial addition in accordance with Greek and reports differing Ethiopic evidence. The selected printed text says no tree was planted; it does not assert a forest or the absence of every kind of vegetation.

translation.text: And I marveled at the rocks, and I marveled at the valley, and I marveled greatly.[a]

footnotes.text: The singular landscape term translated “valley” can also be rendered “ravine.” The threefold expression of wonder is retained.
